inputs.query: What is the history of Zephyr Mosaics, who founded it, and what is its flagship product?

docs.zephyr_company.txt:
Zephyr Mosaics company profile

Zephyr Mosaics is a small glass-tile manufacturer. It was founded in 2009 in Tallinn, Estonia, by the ceramic artist Kaja Rebane, who had previously restored church windows. The company started in a rented boathouse workshop with four employees.

By 2023 Zephyr Mosaics employed 140 people and exported to 22 countries. Its second factory opened in Tartu in 2019.
docs.zephyr_products.txt:
Zephyr Mosaics product notes

The flagship product of Zephyr Mosaics is the Aurora Tessera, an iridescent 2 cm glass tile launched in 2017. The Aurora Tessera is made from 60 percent recycled bottle glass and is fired at 780 degrees Celsius.

Other lines include the Fjord Matte series (2012) and the custom mural service.

vorna-overview.title: Lake Vorna: an overview
vorna-overview.text:
Lake Vorna is a cold mountain lake in the fictional Ostrava Highlands. Its best-known fish is the silver char, a small salmonid that spawns on gravel beds in the lake's northern bay.

The lake is fed by the Kell river and has a maximum depth of 84 metres.

vorna-char-decline.title: Silver char decline in Lake Vorna
vorna-char-decline.text:
Surveys of the silver char in Lake Vorna found the spawning population fell by about 70 percent between 1998 and 2015. Researchers at the Ostrava Fisheries Institute traced the decline to sediment from the Kell river dam, built in 1996, which smothered the gravel spawning beds in the northern bay.

Introduced perch competing for food were a secondary cause.

vorna-restoration.title: Restoring spawning beds at Lake Vorna
vorna-restoration.text:
In 2018 the regional council started the Vorna Gravel Project, placing 3,000 tonnes of clean gravel on the northern bay spawning grounds and opening a sediment bypass at the Kell river dam.

By 2023 the silver char spawning count had recovered to roughly half of its 1998 level.

inputs.query: What are the main design features of the Kestrel-9 programming language?

kestrel-intro.title: Introducing Kestrel-9
kestrel-intro.text:
Kestrel-9 is a statically typed programming language first released in 2021 by the Halvard Compiler Group. Programs are organised into units called perches, and every perch compiles to a single WebAssembly module.

Kestrel-9 uses significant indentation and has no null value; optional values use the Maybe type.

kestrel-memory.title: Memory management in Kestrel-9
kestrel-memory.text:
Kestrel-9 manages memory with region-based allocation rather than a garbage collector. Each function call opens a region, called a nest, which is freed in one step when the call returns.

Values that must outlive a nest are moved explicitly with the keyword carry.

kestrel-rumours.title: Kestrel-9 forum rumours
kestrel-rumours.text: Some forum users claim that Kestrel-9 has a garbage collector and was released in 2015 by a company named Brightwing. These claims are unsourced. Kestrel-9 design features and the programming language history are debated here.

The Brannoch Observatory

The Brannoch Observatory sits on Carn Liath in the Scottish Highlands. It was founded by the amateur astronomer Isobel MacRury and opened to the public in 1931.

Its main instrument is a refracting telescope with an aperture of 61 cm, installed in 1934 and restored in 2008.

inputs.query: How is the Quillfeather Bakery cooperative organised and how are profits shared?

langchain_documents.text: Quillfeather Bakery is a worker cooperative in Ghent, Belgium, founded in 2014. Each of its 31 worker-members holds one vote, and a seven-member council is elected every two years.

Quillfeather Bakery splits its annual surplus three ways: 40 percent is paid to members in proportion to hours worked, 35 percent goes to a reserve fund, and 25 percent funds a community bread programme for local schools.

inputs.query: How did the Brask Valley railway change the economy of Holm Ferry between 1880 and 1930?

brask-railway.title: The Brask Valley railway
brask-railway.text: The Brask Valley railway opened in 1884 and linked the river town of Holm Ferry to the coal port of Ostrand. It was built by the Brask Valley Railway Company, whose chief engineer was Elin Sauder.

holm-ferry-economy.title: Holm Ferry economy, 1880-1930
holm-ferry-economy.text: Before the railway, Holm Ferry lived on river barge traffic and cattle markets. After 1884 three timber mills opened beside the station, and the town's population grew from 2,100 in 1880 to 6,800 in 1930. The barge trade collapsed by 1900 because rail freight to Ostrand was cheaper.

brask-railway.text:
The Brask Valley railway opened in 1884 and linked the river town of Holm Ferry to the coal port of Ostrand. It was built by the Brask Valley Railway Company, whose chief engineer was Elin Sauder.

The line was 41 kilometres long and closed to passengers in 1962.
